_comment: EXAMPLE · SQL Server source / incremental — a parameterised query with a persisted watermark. THE THREE PIECES: bind the cursor as `:name` (a typed statement parameter, never string interpolation); seed it with initial_values (FIRST RUN ONLY — every run reads ctx.get_attr first and falls back, so editing the seed does not rewind); advance it with ctx.set_attr from the batch you just published, reading the new value with max_for() (the top-ranking row's columns as a dict; several columns = a composite cursor). THE NO-RESULTS RULE is read_always_empty: when the slot is None leave the watermark ALONE and return None — a `set_attr(wm, 0)` fallback in that branch is the classic bug that re-ingests everything every time the source goes quiet. Four publishers: read_watermark_by_id (one page per run — RUN IT REPEATEDLY), read_composite_watermark, read_several_binds (a bind as a re-tunable knob, not only a cursor), read_always_empty. Dialect: `OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY`. One function per file under functions/mssql_src_incremental/. Run: `tdd xp one-shot --suite examples/mssql_src_incremental --keep`, then run-triggers again.
